title: Four New Insights About the Coronavirus

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我是安德鲁·罗斯-索尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for Dealbook, a daily newsletter at the
sentences.zh: 我负责《纽约时报》每日简报 Dealbook 的商业与政策报道。

sentences.en: New York Times.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市 Dealbook 峰会的现场采访商业、政治和文化领域最具影响力的几位领袖，包括 J·D·

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜·

sentences.en: Lagarde, Zylran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the Dealbook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 拉加德、齐尔兰·蒙达尼以及许多其他人。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 你可以实时观看其中一些毫无防备、未经过滤的对话。

sentences.en: We're going to be live-streaming select interviews for anyone to watch free at nytimes.com on November 18th.
sentences.zh: 我们将于11月18日在 nytimes.com 上直播精选采访，供任何人免费观看。

sentences.en: If you're not already a subscriber, you can download the New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是订阅者，你可以下载《纽约时报》应用程序来观看，并获得我们所有新闻内容一个月的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 我希望大家能收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 你一定不想错过。

sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是来自《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴尔巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily, today.
sentences.zh: 这里是《每日新闻》，今天。

sentences.en: As infection rates break new records across the U.S.
sentences.zh: 随着全美感染率创下新纪录

sentences.en: this July 4th weekend, four new insights into the virus.
sentences.zh: 在这个7月4日的周末，关于这种病毒的四个新见解。

sentences.en: From my colleague, science reporter Donald G.
sentences.zh: 来自我的同事、科学记者唐纳德·G·

sentences.en: McNeil Jr.
sentences.zh: 麦克尼尔小（Donald G. McNeil Jr.）。

sentences.en: It's Monday, July 6th.
sentences.zh: 今天是7月6日，星期一。

sentences.en: Well, let me start by Donald saying happy 4th of July.
sentences.zh: 那么，唐纳德，请允许我先祝你7月4日国庆快乐。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你。

sentences.en: How did you spend it?
sentences.zh: 你是怎么度过的？

sentences.en: Saturday, I played softball in the morning, socially distanced softball.
sentences.zh: 周六早上我打了一场垒球，保持社交距离的垒球。

sentences.en: Softball?
sentences.zh: 垒球？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: In New York City?
sentences.zh: 在纽约市？

sentences.en: In New York City, yeah, at Riverside Park.
sentences.zh: 在纽约市，对，在河滨公园。

sentences.en: And then we went to dinner last night in a friend's backyard on Long Island, where we all sat as couples together, but six feet apart from each
sentences.zh: 然后昨晚我们去长岛一个朋友的后院吃晚饭，我们所有人都以夫妻为单位坐在一起，但彼此保持着六英尺的距离

sentences.en: other and sort of took turns going up to the table to get to the food and sat and, you know, had a really nice time.
sentences.zh: 轮流走到桌前去拿食物，坐下来，你知道的，度过了非常美好的一段时光。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: I have to imagine that even a socially distanced meal with you
sentences.zh: 我不得不想象，即使是跟你保持社交距离的用餐

sentences.en: is challenging and that I think I would feel quite seen and judged, given your role.
sentences.zh: 也是充满挑战的，而且考虑到你的角色，我想我会觉得自己被彻底看穿和评判了。

sentences.en: Why?
sentences.zh: 为什么？

sentences.en: I mean, I do tend to say six feet, six feet, six feet, a lot of people.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我确实经常对很多人说：六英尺，六英尺，六英尺。

sentences.en: See?
sentences.zh: 看吧？

sentences.en: Because masks give people a false sense of security.
sentences.zh: 因为口罩会给人一种虚假的安全感。

sentences.en: I mean, this is a big thing on the softball field, is that people would both put on masks and they'd sit next to each other in the
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，垒球场上的一件大事就是，人们既戴着口罩，又坐在休息区相邻的位置

sentences.en: dugout making up the batting order and stuff like that.
sentences.zh: 排定打击顺序诸如此类的。

sentences.en: And I'd go, no, air leaks out of the side of your masks.
sentences.zh: 而我会说：不，空气会从你口罩的两侧漏出来。

sentences.en: And you're not always wearing masks.
sentences.zh: 而且你们并不总是戴着口罩。

sentences.en: Sometimes you're wearing it as a sort of a Captain Ahab blue beard under your chin.
sentences.zh: 有时你们把它当成亚哈船长式的落腮胡那样挂在下巴下面。

sentences.en: So it's better to stay six feet apart.
sentences.zh: 所以最好还是保持六英尺的距离。

sentences.en: That way, if your masks-
sentences.zh: 这样一来，如果你们的口罩——

sentences.en: Do you remember a couple seconds ago how you asked me why it might be challenging to have a meal with you?
sentences.zh: 你还记得几秒钟前你是怎么问我为什么跟你吃饭可能会具有挑战性吗？

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: Touche.
sentences.zh: 说得好。

sentences.en: Touche.
sentences.zh: 说得好。

sentences.en: So everything you just described, of course, is occurring in New York, where the infection rate has been generally declining or at least stabilizing.
sentences.zh: 所以你刚才描述的一切，当然都发生在纽约，那里的感染率总体上一直在下降或至少趋于稳定。

sentences.en: So let's talk about the state of the pandemic in the rest of the country.
sentences.zh: 那么我们来谈谈美国其他地区的疫情状况吧。

sentences.en: I wonder if you can give us a quick status update on this end of the July 4th weekend.
sentences.zh: 我想知道你能不能在这个7月4日周末的尾声给我们做一个快速的现状更新。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: I think it's 39 states now have cases going up.
sentences.zh: 我想现在有39个州的病例在上升。

sentences.en: And, you know, it's hitting hardest in the South and in the WeSt. Texas, Florida, Arizona, California, a number of other states.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，南部和西部受到的打击最重。得克萨斯州、佛罗里达州、亚利桑那州、加利福尼亚州以及其他许多州。

sentences.en: And it's exactly what was predicted, you know, back in May when states were debating opening by Memorial Day, all public health experts said, if you open up when your case counts
sentences.zh: 这完全在预料之中，你知道，早在5月份各州讨论在阵亡将士纪念日之前重新开放时，所有公共卫生专家就都说过，如果你在病例数

sentences.en: are rising, they're going to continue rising and start rising even faster.
sentences.zh: 不断上升的时候重新开放，病例数将继续上升，并且会开始上升得更快。

sentences.en: And now we're seeing that.
sentences.zh: 现在我们正在见证这一点。

sentences.en: For example, in Houston, doctors who knew the situation in New York are saying that what's happening there looks like what happened in New York in early April.
sentences.zh: 例如，在休斯顿，了解纽约情况的医生们表示，那里发生的事情看起来就像4月初纽约发生的情况一样。

sentences.en: Finding new beds, finding ventilators, lots of patients who were sick, patients who were on oxygen, not as many dying yet.
sentences.zh: 寻找新的病床，寻找呼吸机，大量生病的患者，吸氧的患者，虽然死亡人数还没那么多。

sentences.en: But with people on oxygen and on ventilators, they may find themselves in the situation where they have to park refrigerated trucks behind the hospitals to hold the bodies
sentences.zh: 但随着患者吸氧并使用呼吸机，他们可能会发现自己不得不像纽约那样，在医院后面停放冷藏卡车来存放尸体

sentences.en: as they did in New York.
sentences.zh: 的情况。

sentences.en: So, Donald, correct me if I'm wrong.
sentences.zh: 所以，唐纳德，如果我错了请纠正我。

sentences.en: I think the U.S.
sentences.zh: 我想美国

sentences.en: is at about 50,000 infections a day right now.
sentences.zh: 目前的感染人数大约是每天5万例。

sentences.en: Dr. Anthony Fauci said we could get up to 100,000.
sentences.zh: 安东尼·福奇博士说过我们可能会达到10万例。

sentences.en: And if that's a case,
sentences.zh: 如果真是这样的话，

sentences.en: what do we expect the attendant death count to start to look like in the U.S.?
sentences.zh: 我们预计美国的伴随死亡人数会开始变成什么样？

sentences.en: I assume that's going to catch up with that.
sentences.zh: 我假设那也会随之攀升。

sentences.en: Yeah, it'll catch up with it.
sentences.zh: 是的，它会赶上来的。

sentences.en: I mean, but there's no reason to believe that 100,000 is the upper limit.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，但没有理由相信10万就是上限。

sentences.en: It all depends on how much social distancing we practice.
sentences.zh: 这完全取决于我们实行了多少社交距离。

sentences.en: I mean, this is the dance.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这就是这场博弈。

sentences.en: And do you close bars and restaurants?
sentences.zh: 你要关闭酒吧和餐馆吗？

sentences.en: Do you open or close schools?
sentences.zh: 你要开放还是关闭学校？

sentences.en: Do you wear masks?
sentences.zh: 你要戴口罩吗？

sentences.en: How much attention do people pay to the directions you give them?
sentences.zh: 人们对你给他们的指示有多重视？

sentences.en: How much, you know, do they practice good social distancing?
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他们有多大程度上在践行良好的社交距离？

sentences.en: You know, that very much affects the rate of spread of the virus.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这极大地影响了病毒的传播速度。

sentences.en: Well, with that in mind, those big questions of kind of how we proceed through the rest of this
sentences.zh: 好吧，考虑到这一点，关于我们如何度过这场大流行余下阶段的那些重大问题，

sentences.en: pandemic, you have been doing a lot of reporting about the latest learnings and insights into the virus that will very much guide how we answer those questions.
sentences.zh: 你一直在做大量关于这种病毒最新认知和见解的报道，这些报道将在很大程度上指导我们如何回答这些问题。

sentences.en: And we want to talk through those with you.
sentences.zh: 我们想和你一起探讨这些问题。

sentences.en: So where do you think we should start?
sentences.zh: 所以你觉得我们应该从哪里开始？

sentences.en: Some of these insights are really more theories with some evidence to them.
sentences.zh: 其中一些见解其实更像是带有某些证据的理论。

sentences.en: And some there's quite a bit of confidence in.
sentences.zh: 而有些则具有相当高的把握度。

sentences.en: And so we probably ought to start with something that there's a pretty high degree of confidence in among doctors.
sentences.zh: 所以我们大概应该从医生们对此有相当高把握度的事情开始。

sentences.en: And what is that?
sentences.zh: 那是什么？

sentences.en: When this all started, we thought of it as a lung disease, a respiratory disease, because the first cases we heard about, people got pneumonia.
sentences.zh: 这一切刚开始时，我们认为它是一种肺部疾病、一种呼吸道疾病，因为我们听说的第一批病例中，人们都得了肺炎。

sentences.en: And that, of course, reminded us that the model for this disease was the 1918 influenza epidemic.
sentences.zh: 当然，这让我们想起这种疾病的模板是1918年的流感大流行。

sentences.en: But we're learning that this coronavirus is very different from an influenza virus.
sentences.zh: 但我们现在了解到，这种冠状病毒与流感病毒截然不同。

sentences.en: The influenza virus is attached to receptors in the lungs and the airway.
sentences.zh: 流感病毒附着在肺部和气道的受体上。

sentences.en: This gets into the body through the airway, through the lungs, but it really attaches to the insides of the blood vessels.
sentences.zh: 而这种病毒通过气道和肺部进入人体，但它真正附着的是血管内部。

sentences.en: And so that makes it a vascular disease, a blood vessel disease.
sentences.zh: 因此，这使其成为一种血管疾病。

sentences.en: And what are the implications of a virus like this being a vascular disease, a blood vessel disease, and not just a respiratory disease?
sentences.zh: 像这样的病毒是一种血管疾病（而不仅仅是一种呼吸道疾病），这意味着什么？

sentences.en: It means it affects every organ in the body that has lots of fine blood vessels in it, and not even just organs.
sentences.zh: 这意味着它会影响体内所有拥有大量微细血管的器官，甚至不仅仅是器官。

sentences.en: I mean, so it affects the lungs, which are the filter where the air gets into the blood,
sentences.zh: 我是说，它会影响肺部，肺部是空气进入血液的过滤器，

sentences.en: and you have lots of little fine blood vessels surrounding the little sacks at the ends of your breathing tubes.
sentences.zh: 并且你的呼吸管道末端的小气囊周围有许多微小而纤细的血管。

sentences.en: It attacks the kidneys because that's the filter where the urine comes out of the blood.
sentences.zh: 它会攻击肾脏，因为那是尿液从血液中滤出的过滤器。

sentences.en: So you have very fine networks of blood vessels there.
sentences.zh: 所以那里有非常精细的血管网络。

sentences.en: It attacks the gut because you have a network of blood vessels in your gut where food gets into your body.
sentences.zh: 它会攻击肠道，因为你的肠道里有一个血管网络，食物由此进入你的身体。

sentences.en: It attacks the brain because you have lots of fine blood vessels in the brain.
sentences.zh: 它会攻击大脑，因为你的大脑中有许多微细的血管。

sentences.en: It doesn't attack the nerve cells in the brain, which most of the brain is made of.
sentences.zh: 它不攻击大脑中的神经细胞（大脑大部分由神经细胞构成）。

sentences.en: It doesn't attack the muscle cells in the heart, but it attacks the blood vessels that go through all those other parts.
sentences.zh: 它不攻击心脏的肌肉细胞，但它会攻击穿过所有这些其他部位的血管。

sentences.en: And so when they do autopsies, they find like thousands of tiny little blood clots all over the body.
sentences.zh: 因此，当他们进行尸检时，他们会在全身发现数千个微小的血栓。

sentences.en: You have lots of people who have strokes, and as those blood clots clot up blood vessels to small areas of the brain, you may get dementia or disorientation.
sentences.zh: 有很多人会中风，随着这些血栓堵塞大脑小区域的血管，你可能会出现痴呆或定向障碍。

sentences.en: And then in kids, when you have COVID toes in teenagers and young adults, this is the little capillaries in the hands and feet getting blocked and getting this
sentences.zh: 然后对于儿童，当你在青少年和年轻人身上看到“新冠脚趾”时，这是手脚中的微血管被阻塞，并出现这种

sentences.en: inflamed, painful, red or purple toe and finger syndrome.
sentences.zh: 发炎、疼痛、红肿或发紫的脚趾和手指综合征。

sentences.en: So it's just, it's more complicated to deal with a disease that can travel to any organ in the body.
sentences.zh: 所以，处理一种能够传播到体内任何器官的疾病要复杂得多。

sentences.en: So how does this new insight about the coronavirus, how does it change the way we are going to approach the pandemic?
sentences.zh: 那么关于冠状病毒的这一新见解，它将如何改变我们对待这场大流行的方式？

sentences.en: Before, the main thing you're looking for when you're looking to see if somebody's having a problem
sentences.zh: 在此之前，当你想要查看某人是否遇到问题时，你主要寻找的是

sentences.en: is their blood oxygen level, because you're assuming that their problem is going to be pneumonia.
sentences.zh: 他们的血氧水平，因为你假设他们的问题会是肺炎。

sentences.en: But if you realize that the problem could be kidney damage, heart damage, you do a whole different battery of blood tests.
sentences.zh: 但如果你意识到问题可能是肾损伤、心脏损伤，你就会做一套完全不同的血液检查。

sentences.en: So what you're saying is that doctors who previously were diagnosing COVID-19 through a
sentences.zh: 所以你的意思是，以前通过一套成熟的症状来诊断 COVID-19 的医生们，

sentences.en: set of well-established symptoms, right, now need to expand that set of symptoms pretty broadly, because it turns out this is looking to be vascular, not respiratory.
sentences.zh: 现在需要大大扩展这些症状的范围，因为事实证明这看起来是血管疾病，而不是呼吸道疾病。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's right.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: It means that virtually anybody who comes into a doctor's office feeling sick might have the coronavirus.
sentences.zh: 这意味着几乎任何走进诊所感觉不舒服的人都可能感染了冠状病毒。

sentences.en: If they come in with symptoms of a stroke, it might be COVID.
sentences.zh: 如果他们带着中风的症状来，那可能是新冠。

sentences.en: If they come in with symptoms of a heart attack, it might be COVID.
sentences.zh: 如果他们带着心脏病的症状来，那可能是新冠。

sentences.en: If they come in with what seems like arthritis in their feet, you know, it might be COVID toe.
sentences.zh: 如果他们带着脚部看似关节炎的症状来，你知道的，那可能是“新冠脚趾”。

sentences.en: And because we often don't have enough tests, or it takes a long time to get test results, the patient's at a real disadvantage, because
sentences.zh: 而且由于我们通常没有足够的检测，或者获取检测结果需要很长时间，患者处于非常不利的境地，因为

sentences.en: if you don't know your patient has coronavirus, whatever symptom they've got now might
sentences.zh: 如果你不知道你的患者患有冠状病毒，他们现在拥有的任何症状可能

sentences.en: become greater, might spread to other organs.
sentences.zh: 会加重，可能会扩散到其他器官。

sentences.en: So the problem in your toes might literally spread to your kidneys or your brain.
sentences.zh: 所以你脚趾上的问题可能会字面意义上扩散到你的肾脏或大脑。

sentences.en: And you want to know that that patient has a disease that can spread throughout the body.
sentences.zh: 而你会希望知道该患者患有一种可以扩散到全身的疾病。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: In other words, more testing, fast testing becomes more imperative once we have learned that so many symptoms may actually be a sign of COVID-19.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，一旦我们了解到如此多的症状实际上可能是 COVID-19 的迹象，更多的检测、快速的检测就变得更加势在必行。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是的。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So what is the next big new insight we have into the coronavirus?
sentences.zh: 那么我们对冠状病毒的下一个重大新见解是什么？

sentences.en: Well, people are always asking, is the virus mutating?
sentences.zh: 人们总是在问：病毒在变异吗？

sentences.en: Is it becoming different?
sentences.zh: 它在变得不同吗？

sentences.en: And the answer is yes, this virus always mutates.
sentences.zh: 答案是肯定的，这种病毒一直在变异。

sentences.en: It makes one mutation about every two weeks.
sentences.zh: 它大约每两周发生一次变异。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: The question is, are any of those mutations important?
sentences.zh: 问题是，这些变异中哪怕有任何一个是重要的吗？

sentences.en: And most of them aren't.
sentences.zh: 大多数都不是。

sentences.en: Most of them don't change the function of the virus at all.
sentences.zh: 它们大多根本没有改变病毒的功能。

sentences.en: But there has been one mutation that has become the object of a great deal of intereSt. We know for sure that there are sort of two general
sentences.zh: 但确实有一种变异已经成为人们极度关注的对象。我们确切地知道，这种病毒大致有两种主要

sentences.en: clades of the virus, the Wuhan strain and the other one called the Italian strain or sometimes the
sentences.zh: 进化枝，即武汉毒株和另一种被称为意大利毒株或有时被称为

sentences.en: European strain.
sentences.zh: 欧洲毒株的毒株。

sentences.en: Now, the Wuhan strain is obviously the original one.
sentences.zh: 现在，武汉毒株显然是最初的那种。

sentences.en: That's where the virus started.
sentences.zh: 那是病毒起源的地方。

sentences.en: But, you know, it went around Asia, then it went to Iran, then it went to Italy.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道的，它传遍了亚洲，然后传到了伊朗，接着传到了意大利。

sentences.en: And in Italy, sometime in February, presumably, this mutation took place.
sentences.zh: 在意大利，大概在2月份的某个时候，这种变异发生了。

sentences.en: Now, it has definitely not made the virus more dangerous, more lethal, more likely to kill you.
sentences.zh: 现在，它绝对没有让病毒变得更危险、更致命、更有可能致死。

sentences.en: But it appears to have made it more transmissible.
sentences.zh: 但它似乎让病毒更容易传播了。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 唔。

sentences.en: How so?
sentences.zh: 怎么说？

sentences.en: Well, it appears that it transmits between people five to ten times more easily.
sentences.zh: 嗯，它似乎在人与人之间传播的容易程度增加了五到十倍。

sentences.en: Now, this is in dispute, but there's been work done in cells in the laboratory where they infected them with the two different strains.
sentences.zh: 现在，这一点尚存争议，但在实验室的细胞中已经开展了相关工作，他们用这两种不同的毒株感染了细胞。

sentences.en: And the mutation in the Italian strain seems to make the spikes on the outside of the virus, the spikes of the corona, more stable, better able to infect.
sentences.zh: 意大利毒株中的变异似乎使病毒外部的突起（即冠状病毒的刺突）更加稳定，更有能力感染细胞。

sentences.en: And so that they appear to be five to ten times more capable at infecting cells as the old Wuhan version.
sentences.zh: 因此，与旧的武汉版本相比，它们似乎具备了五到十倍感染细胞的能力。

sentences.en: So the strain of this virus that has a better spike, the Italian strain, and is therefore more
sentences.zh: 所以这种刺突蛋白更好的病毒株，也就是意大利变异株，因其更具

sentences.en: transmissible, is crowding out the previous strain because it's just doing a better, more effective job of infecting people.
sentences.zh: 传染性，正在排挤之前的毒株，因为它在感染人类这方面做得更好、更有效。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's right.
sentences.zh: 对，没错。

sentences.en: It's the natural progression for a virus.
sentences.zh: 这是病毒的自然演变过程。

sentences.en: It's the way they tend to go.
sentences.zh: 这是它们通常的发展方向。

sentences.en: What do you mean?
sentences.zh: 你是什么意思？

sentences.en: Well, viruses over the course of infecting lots of hosts tend to become less lethal to those hosts and more transmissible.
sentences.zh: 嗯，病毒在感染大量宿主的过程中，往往会对这些宿主毒性变小，而传染性变强。

sentences.en: Like, for example, if I have the virus and it mutates inside me and it turns into a more deadly strain, I've now got two strains, and I pass on that virus to two
sentences.zh: 比如，如果我感染了病毒，它在我体内发生突变，变成了一种毒性更强的毒株，我现在有了两种毒株，然后我把病毒传给两

sentences.en: people, the person who gets the more deadly strain is more likely to go home, go to bed, and die.
sentences.zh: 个人，感染了更致命毒株的那个人更有可能回家，上床睡觉，然后死去。

sentences.en: Whereas the person who gets the less lethal, more transmissible strain is going to go out to a disco and infect 40 people.
sentences.zh: 而感染了毒性较低、传染性较强毒株的那个人则会去迪厅，并传染40个人。

sentences.en: And if you do that enough times in the course of the virus, the virus always sort of naturally moves in the direction of the more transmissible, less lethal one, because that's
sentences.zh: 如果在病毒的传播过程中发生足够多次这样的情况，病毒总是会自然而然地朝传染性更强、毒性更弱的方向发展，因为这就是

sentences.en: the one that spreads whenever it's given that kind of fork in the road.
sentences.zh: 当面临这种分岔路口时，它会选择扩散的方向。

sentences.en: And so this is what happened in 1918.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是1918年发生的事情。

sentences.en: The virus started off extremely deadly.
sentences.zh: 这种病毒一开始极其致命。

sentences.en: It blew through an enormous chunk of the population, probably 60 to 70% of all the people in the world.
sentences.zh: 它席卷了庞大的人口比例，可能占全世界所有人口的60%到70%。

sentences.en: And then it disappeared for a while.
sentences.zh: 然后它消失了一段时间。

sentences.en: Then it turned up in pigs, and it was a pig virus for a while.
sentences.zh: 接着它在猪身上出现，并在一段时间内成为一种猪病毒。

sentences.en: And then when enough humans who'd never had the virus were born, it reappeared in people.
sentences.zh: 然后，当足够多从未感染过该病毒的人类出生时，它又在人群中重新出现。

sentences.en: But it reappeared as the H1N1 seasonal flu, the one that we know about is one of the seasonal flus every year.
sentences.zh: 但它重新出现时变成了H1N1季节性流感，也就是我们所知道的每年季节性流感中的一种。

sentences.en: But that virus became less lethal and more transmissible.
sentences.zh: 但那种病毒变得毒性减弱、传染性增强。

sentences.en: And basically all viruses do that.
sentences.zh: 基本上所有病毒都是这样。

sentences.en: And we might be beginning to see the very first hints of that happening with this virus.
sentences.zh: 而我们可能开始看到这种病毒发生这种情况的最初迹象。

sentences.en: So if I'm in Texas or Arizona right now, and I'm testing positive for
sentences.zh: 所以如果我现在在得克萨斯州或亚利桑那州，并且我

sentences.en: COVID-19, it sounds quite likely that I've gotten the Italian mutation of this virus, right?
sentences.zh: 新冠病毒检测呈阳性，听起来我很有可能感染了这种病毒的意大利变异株，对吧？

sentences.en: And that means I'm quite likely to spread it to somebody else and not have the most horrible symptoMs.
sentences.zh: 这意味着我很有可能把它传染给别人，而且不会出现最可怕的症状。

sentences.en: So does that partly help explain why infection rates are rising so rapidly in the US?
sentences.zh: 那么，这是否在一定程度上有助于解释为什么美国的感染率上升得如此之快？

sentences.en: Well, infection rates are rising rapidly in the US more because of human behavior than because of any changes in the virus.
sentences.zh: 嗯，美国感染率迅速上升，更多是因为人类的行为，而不是因为病毒本身的任何变化。

sentences.en: I think it's wishful.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一种厢情愿。

sentences.en: I mean, it's wishful thinking to think that this virus is not dangerous.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，认为这种病毒不危险是一厢情愿的想法。

sentences.en: It's really dangerous.
sentences.zh: 它真的很危险。

sentences.en: And it's highly transmissible.
sentences.zh: 而且它的传染性极高。

sentences.en: But because the Italian version of the virus spreads more effectively, that does suggest that
sentences.zh: 但由于意大利版本的病毒传播得更有效，这确实表明

sentences.en: the virus is becoming better at doing the thing it was designed to do, which is to infect lots and lots of people.
sentences.zh: 病毒在做它被设计要做的事情方面变得更好了，那就是感染成千上万的人。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But I mean, the Italian version versus the Wuhan version isn't the dead end.
sentences.zh: 但我的意思是，意大利版本对比武汉版本并不是终点。

sentences.en: There are going to be many more mutations.
sentences.zh: 还会有更多的突变。

sentences.en: It mutates every two weeks.
sentences.zh: 它每两周突变一次。

sentences.en: There may be other mutations turning up in the virus that turn out to be important.
sentences.zh: 病毒中可能会出现其他被证明很重要的突变。

sentences.en: And we may call those the Texas strain or the
sentences.zh: 我们可能会把这些称为得克萨斯变异株或

sentences.en: California strain or whatever, but we don't know them yet.
sentences.zh: 加利福尼亚变异株之类的，但我们现在还不知道。

sentences.en: There's a lot of disagreement about this.
sentences.zh: 对此有很多分歧。

sentences.en: This is among scientists there, you know, as to whether or not it really is more transmissible.
sentences.zh: 科学家之间就是这样，你知道的，关于它是否真的更具传染性。

sentences.en: And there's zero agreement that it not even really any thought that it's less dangerous.
sentences.zh: 并且完全没有共识，甚至几乎没有人认为它毒性较小。

sentences.en: That completely remains to be seen.
sentences.zh: 这完全拭目以待。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: The New York Times app unlocked.
sentences.zh: 纽约时报App已解锁。

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to the Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 大家都知道，你需要订阅《时报》才能阅读所有报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore the Times for a month for free without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但是，如果你能免费试用《时报》一个月而无需输入信用卡信息呢？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在你可以了。

sentences.en: When you download the New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 当你第一次下载纽约时报App时，你在App里的第一个月是免费的。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 有一个月的时间可以突破付费墙，看看《时报》订阅者每天都能获得什么。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to the New York Times, download the Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果你还没有订阅纽约时报，请立即下载时报App并获得30天的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: So Don, what is the next big new understanding we have into the virus at this point?
sentences.zh: 那么唐，我们目前对病毒的下一个重大新理解是什么？

sentences.en: Well, there's more and more confirmation that you are much safer outdoors than you are indoors.
sentences.zh: 嗯，越来越多的证据证实，在户外比在室内安全得多。

sentences.en: There's a study in China that looked at 318 clusters of transmission and only one case involved outdoor transmission.
sentences.zh: 中国的一项研究调查了318个传播集群，其中只有一起涉及户外传播。

sentences.en: And that was between two neighbors who had a long conversation with each other.
sentences.zh: 那是两个彼此进行了长时间交谈的邻居之间发生的。

sentences.en: And there's recently been another study from Japan that suggests that your chances of getting the virus indoors are 20 times as high as it would be outdoors.
sentences.zh: 日本最近的另一项研究表明，你在室内感染病毒的几率是在户外的20倍。

sentences.en: And what are these studies finding about why exactly that is?
sentences.zh: 这些研究发现这究竟是为什么？

sentences.en: I mean, I think we all have some understanding that when you're outside, the virus is just going to disperse and become more diffuse.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我想我们都明白，当你在室外时，病毒只会消散并变得更加稀疏。

sentences.en: Is that as copacal as it is?
sentences.zh: 事情真有这么简单吗？

sentences.en: Well, there's always a little bit of wind outside.
sentences.zh: 嗯，室外总是有点风。

sentences.en: I mean, humidity also makes droplets fall out of the air, but mostly it's the wind.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，湿度也会导致飞沫从空气中落下来，但主要是风。

sentences.en: And when people talk within a few feet of each other, especially when they talk loud or when they laugh or when they sing or shout
sentences.zh: 当人们在彼此几英尺的范围内交谈时，尤其是当他们大声说话、大笑、唱歌或喊叫

sentences.en: or do anything like that, you put out this kind of invisible mist of little tiny droplets that spews out
sentences.zh: 或做任何类似的事情时，你就会喷发出这种看不见的小飞沫雾气，从你的嘴里喷出

sentences.en: of your mouth and sort of hangs around your head, but it also drifts towards the other person.
sentences.zh: 并悬浮在你的头部周围，但它也会向另一个人漂去。

sentences.en: And so you're sitting inside each other's droplet cloud.
sentences.zh: 所以你们正坐在彼此的飞沫云中。

sentences.en: And those little tiny droplets, even if you're not feeling the other person in effect spitting on your face, that droplet cloud can hold enough virus to transmit the
sentences.zh: 而那些极小的飞沫，即使你没有感觉到对方实际上在往你脸上吐口水，那个飞沫云也能承载足够的病毒来传播

sentences.en: disease from one person to the other.
sentences.zh: 疾病从一个人传给另一个人。

sentences.en: And indoors, when there's no windows open, it can sort of drift through
sentences.zh: 而在室内，当没有窗户打开时，它会在房间里飘荡

sentences.en: the room, more or less at head level, and go past one person after another at a cocktail party or inside a bar
sentences.zh: 或多或少在头部的高度，在鸡尾酒会或酒吧里依次飘过一个人接一个人

sentences.en: or like that, and each person inhaling a little bit of that droplet cloud until the disease is spread to 20, 30,
sentences.zh: 或者类似的地方，每个人都吸入一点点那个飞沫云，直到疾病传播给20、30、

sentences.en: 40 people.
sentences.zh: 40个人。

sentences.en: Whereas outdoors, the breeze just blows that away.
sentences.zh: 而在户外，微风直接把它吹走了。

sentences.en: So standing six feet away outdoors, even without masks, is considered safe.
sentences.zh: 所以在户外保持六英尺的距离，即使不戴口罩，也被认为是安全的。

sentences.en: This is the idea that the virus becomes aerosolized.
sentences.zh: 这就是病毒变成气溶胶的概念。

sentences.en: And you're saying that indoors, that poses a very significant danger outdoors because of wind, nowhere near as much.
sentences.zh: 你是说在室内，由于这种气溶胶化的病毒雾气，构成了非常重大的危险，而在户外由于有风，危险程度远没有那么高。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's right.
sentences.zh: 对，没错。

sentences.en: So if being outdoors is less risky and it's now been clinically shown, I wonder if that explains
sentences.zh: 所以，如果待在户外风险较小，并且现在已经在临床上得到了证明，我不知道这是否能解释

sentences.en: something you mentioned the last time that we spoke, which is that you did not have a tremendous
sentences.zh: 你上次我们交谈时提到的一件事，那就是你并没有

sentences.en: amount of fear that these protests that have occurred all over the United States over race and policing, that they would be a major source of infection.
sentences.zh: 过分担心全美各地爆发的关于种族和警务的抗议活动会成为主要的感染源。

sentences.en: And is that because they occurred outdoors?
sentences.zh: 这是因为它们发生在户外吗？

sentences.en: And is it so far the case that they haven't led to a meaningful spike in infections?
sentences.zh: 到目前为止，它们没有导致感染的大幅激增，是这样吗？

sentences.en: We have not seen any big spike in infections in the cities where most of the protests took place.
sentences.zh: 在绝大多数抗议活动发生的城市里，我们没有看到任何感染的大幅激增。

sentences.en: So it looks like they didn't lead to a lot of transmission.
sentences.zh: 所以看起来它们并没有导致大量的传播。

sentences.en: That doesn't imply that everything is safe just because it's outdoors.
sentences.zh: 这并不意味着只要在户外一切都是安全的。

sentences.en: The important thing is how far apart people are when they're outdoors.
sentences.zh: 重要的事情是人们在户外时的间距有多远。

sentences.en: So sitting right next to somebody else in, you know, in front of a stage at Mount Rushmore, for example, where the chairs are zip-tied together, is not safe.
sentences.zh: 所以，例如，紧挨着另一个人坐在拉什莫尔山的一个舞台前，那里的椅子是用扎带绑在一起的，这是不安全的。

sentences.en: Masks or no masks, you still really want to try to keep six feet distance.
sentences.zh: 戴不戴口罩，你其实都真的想要尽量保持六英尺的距离。

sentences.en: Donald, a couple of moments ago, you mentioned the danger of being indoors because of this aerosolized virus mist that is not as great a danger outdoors.
sentences.zh: 唐，刚才你提到了在室内因为这种气溶胶化的病毒雾气而带来的危险，这在户外并没有那么大的危险。

sentences.en: But I want to linger on this question of the indoors for a moment.
sentences.zh: 但我还想纠结于这个室内的问题一会儿。

sentences.en: Because the more we think about it, that aerosolized mist would seem to make any indoor activity inherently dangerous.
sentences.zh: 因为越想越觉得，那种气溶胶化的雾气似乎会让任何室内活动都具有内在的危险性。

sentences.en: I wonder if that's an accurate assessment.
sentences.zh: 我想知道这是否是一个准确的评估。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, we've seen transmission of virus to large numbers of people in funerals, in choir
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们已经看到病毒在葬礼、唱诗班

sentences.en: practices, at birthday parties, inside bars, in business meetings, virtually any kind of indoor environment you can imagine.
sentences.zh: 练习、生日派对、酒吧内部、商务会议以及你可以想象的几乎任何类型的室内环境中传播给大量的人。

sentences.en: There have been super spreader events.
sentences.zh: 已经发生了很多超级传播事件。

sentences.en: There may be ways to eventually make indoor spaces safer.
sentences.zh: 最终可能会有办法让室内空间更安全。

sentences.en: There's going to be no way to make them completely safe.
sentences.zh: 但没有办法让它们变得绝对安全。

sentences.en: And all this talk about what's safe to do indoors brings us to really the most important question, which is the most
sentences.zh: 所有这些关于在室内做什么才安全的讨论，真正把我们带到了最重要的问题上，也就是我们想要恢复运作的最重要的

sentences.en: important indoor space we want to get functioning again, which is schools.
sentences.zh: 室内空间，那就是学校。

sentences.en: Can kids go to school safely?
sentences.zh: 孩子们能安全地上学吗？

sentences.en: And again, the science isn't firm yet, but there are more and more hints that it may be safe or pretty safe to open the schools in the fall, especially for very young kids.
sentences.zh: 同样，科学结论还未定论，但越来越多的迹象表明，在秋季重新开学可能是安全或相当安全的，尤其是对很小的孩子而言。

sentences.en: There's growing evidence that kids are not big transmitters of the virus to adults.
sentences.zh: 越来越多的证据表明，孩子不是将病毒传播给成人的主要群体。

sentences.en: Denmark opened its schools in April, did not see a big spike up in cases.
sentences.zh: 丹麦在4月份重新开学，病例没有大幅激增。

sentences.en: Finland opened at schools in May, did not see a big spike up in cases.
sentences.zh: 芬兰在5月份重新开学，病例没有大幅激增。

sentences.en: Even from the beginning in China, the Chinese said, you know, every time they looked at clusters in families, almost never
sentences.zh: 甚至从中国的初期开始，中国就表示，你知道的，每次他们查看家庭集群时，几乎从不

sentences.en: did they see a case where the child, particularly the youngest child, was the one who introduced the virus into the family.
sentences.zh: 看到儿童，尤其是最小的儿童，是将病毒引入家庭的那个案例。

sentences.en: Usually it was parent infecting the kids, not the other way around.
sentences.zh: 通常是父母感染孩子，而不是相反。

sentences.en: We know that kids are big transmitters of flu viruses, and they do it because they cough and sneeze like crazy.
sentences.zh: 我们知道儿童是流感病毒的主要传播者，他们这样做是因为他们疯狂地咳嗽和打喷嚏。

sentences.en: But if the biggest symptom that they're getting is inflammation rather than coughing and sneezing,
sentences.zh: 但如果他们出现的最大症状是炎症而不是咳嗽和打喷嚏，

sentences.en: and that's the case, kids tend to get more sort of cranky, inflammatory, unpleasant manifestations of
sentences.zh: 事实确实如此，孩子们往往会得到更多这种烦躁的、炎症性的、令人不愉快的疾病表现，

sentences.en: the disease rather than something that looks like a cold, then it would make sense that that might be a reason why they're not big transmitters.
sentences.zh: 而不是看起来像感冒的症状，那么这就说得通了，这可能是他们不是主要传播者的原因。

sentences.en: And what does this new insight about kids being less likely to transmit mean for the teachers who are going to stand or sit in front of them all day?
sentences.zh: 那么，关于儿童不太可能传播病毒的这种新见解，对整天站在或坐在他们面前的老师意味着什么？

sentences.en: Does it mean that an adult teacher in a school is pretty safe teaching, or does it not mean that at all?
sentences.zh: 这是否意味着学校里的成年老师教书相当安全，还是根本不是这个意思？

sentences.en: I don't think we know the answer to that yet.
sentences.zh: 我想我们现在还不知道答案。

sentences.en: I mean, schools, you're bringing together a lot of kids, kids, but schools also bring together a lot of adults, teachers, staff, parents, picking up the kids, things like that.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，学校里聚集了许多孩子，但学校也聚集了许多成年人，老师、员工、接孩子的家长，诸如此类。

sentences.en: So schools are not going to be completely safe under any circumstances.
sentences.zh: 因此，在任何情况下，学校都不可能是绝对安全的。

sentences.en: But opening schools is so important to society, much more important than opening restaurants, much more important than opening movie theaters.
sentences.zh: 但重新开学对社会极其重要，比重新开餐厅重要得多，比重新开电影院重要得多。

sentences.en: It probably needs to be done really carefully, not just all back into the classroom, 30 kids to a classroom at all, but it looks like it could be done.
sentences.zh: 它可能需要非常仔细地进行，而不仅仅是全部回到教室，每个教室30个孩子，但看起来它是可以做到的。

sentences.en: And that's really important, because it's important for the kids, for their development, for their feeding, for their socialization.
sentences.zh: 这真的很重要，因为它对孩子们很重要，对他们的发展、饮食、社交都很重要。

sentences.en: And it's also important for the parents.
sentences.zh: 而且对父母也很重要。

sentences.en: Parents can't go back to work if they're stuck at home with their kids.
sentences.zh: 如果父母被困在家里的孩子身边，他们就无法回去工作。

sentences.en: So it's a crucial part of getting both the economy going and just the health of kids and health of parents.
sentences.zh: 因此，这是让经济运转以及保障儿童和父母健康的关键部分。

sentences.en: So of all the insights that you have shared today, this one seems like the silver lining, that reopening schools may be a somewhat safe undertaking.
sentences.zh: 所以，在你今天分享的所有见解中，这一点似乎是阴霾中的一丝曙光，即重新开学可能是一项相对安全的任务。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And that would be very good news for us.
sentences.zh: 这对我们来说将是个非常好的消息。

sentences.en: Because if I'm being candid, everything else you have said sounds pretty bad, right?
sentences.zh: 因为老实说，你所说的一切听起来都很糟糕，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, it seems to be vascular, not respiratory, so it's going to be easy to miss symptoMs.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它似乎是血管性的，而不是呼吸道性的，所以很容易错过症状。

sentences.en: It seems it's becoming more transmissible through mutations, right?
sentences.zh: 看来它正通过突变变得更具传染性，对吧？

sentences.en: And the indoors presents very significant threats for non-kids because of this aerosolized miSt. And once the temperature drops,
sentences.zh: 由于这种气溶胶化的雾气，室内对非儿童构成了非常重大的威胁。一旦气温下降，

sentences.en: which it will do in a few months, and tens of millions of us are suddenly stuck indoors,
sentences.zh: 几个月后就会这样，我们数以千万计的人突然被困在室内，

sentences.en: then we're in for a lot of trouble.
sentences.zh: 那我们就麻烦大了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And the number of cases per day could rise well over 100,000 if we're not careful.
sentences.zh: 如果我们不小心，每天的病例数可能会飙升至远超10万。

sentences.en: So yeah, I guess it's mostly bad news.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，我猜这主要是个坏消息。

sentences.en: Sorry.
sentences.zh: 抱歉。

sentences.en: I'm hoping that the fact that the virus is becoming more transmissible also means that it will become less lethal, which is good news.
sentences.zh: 我希望病毒传染性的增强同时也意味着其毒性的减弱，这是个好消息。

sentences.en: But it hasn't done that yet.
sentences.zh: 但它还没有做到这一点。

sentences.en: So more transmission of a virus that's already bad is not a good thing, no question about it.
sentences.zh: 因此，一种本就糟糕的病毒传染性更强，这绝不是一件好事，毫无疑问。

sentences.en: And all these things that we have just talked about would also seem to reinforce the need, not just for social distancing, but for these government-mandated lockdowns, right?
sentences.zh: 我们刚刚讨论的所有这些事情，似乎也强化了这种需求，不仅是社交距离，还有这些政府强制的封锁，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, specific requirements that say, don't go to a bar, don't go to a restaurant.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，具体的要求是，不要去酒吧，不要去餐厅。

sentences.en: And those will become even more urgent as the warm weather yields to cold weather.
sentences.zh: 随着温暖的天气让位于寒冷的天气，这些要求将变得更加紧迫。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, we have to realize we are just in the opening phases of this pandemic.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们必须意识到我们才刚刚处于这场大流行的初期阶段。

sentences.en: I mean, this is the second inning, and there's still more than 120,000 people dead.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，现在才第二局，而且已经有超过12万人死亡。

sentences.en: So we are doing the dance in, dance out of various forms of lockdown.
sentences.zh: 所以我们在各种形式的封锁中进进出出。

sentences.en: But we need to get to the point where we're all basically dancing to the same music, where all governors accept the notion that when they have a problem
sentences.zh: 但我们需要达到这样一种地步，即我们基本上都随着同一首音乐起舞，所有州长都接受这样一种观念，即当他们的州

sentences.en: that's getting out of control in their state, they react quickly.
sentences.zh: 出现失控的问题时，他们会迅速做出反应。

sentences.en: And if they do that, they will save lives of their own citizens.
sentences.zh: 如果他们这样做，他们就会挽救自己公民的生命。

sentences.en: And I think we're beginning to see that in places like Texas, places like Arizona, places like Florida.
sentences.zh: 我想我们开始在得克萨斯州、亚利桑那州、佛罗里达州等地看到了这一点。

sentences.en: The governors have made major about faces in the last couple of weeks.
sentences.zh: 在过去的两周里，州长们态度发生了重大转变。

sentences.en: And they're getting the science that the thing you do today doesn't produce good effects
sentences.zh: 他们现在明白了，你今天所采取的措施

sentences.en: until a month from today, because the people who got infected yesterday are the ones who are going to be in your hospital three weeks from now.
sentences.zh: 要在一个月后才会显现出效果，因为昨天感染病毒的人，正是三周后会躺进你医院的人。

sentences.en: So they're beginning to catch on, but we need to arrive at sort of a common understanding that we don't all have to move in lockstep as a nation, but at the crucial
sentences.zh: 所以他们开始领悟到了，但我们需要达成某种共识：作为一个国家，我们不必步调完全一致，但在关键

sentences.en: moments, we need to take similar steps to save lives.
sentences.zh: 时刻，我们需要采取相似的行动来拯救生命。

sentences.en: Thank you, Donald.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，唐纳德。

sentences.en: We appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: I was glad to be here.
sentences.zh: 很高兴能来到这里。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天需要了解的其他新闻。

sentences.en: In our schools, our newsrooms, even our corporate boardrooms, there is a new far-left fascism that demands absolute allegiance.
sentences.zh: 在我们的学校、新闻编辑室，甚至企业董事会里，出现了一种要求绝对忠诚的新极左法西斯主义。

sentences.en: In a pair of back-to-back speeches over the weekend,
sentences.zh: 在周末接连发表的两场演讲中，

sentences.en: President Trump delivered harsh attacks against what he called the radical far-left forces who are
sentences.zh: 特朗普总统严厉抨击了他所谓的激进极左势力，

sentences.en: protesting police brutality and tearing down monuments to America's racist past, describing them as a threat to American values and heritage.
sentences.zh: 他们抗议警察暴力执法并推倒美国种族主义过去的纪念碑，特朗普将他们描述为对美国价值观和传统的威胁。

sentences.en: If you do not speak its language, perform its rituals, recite its mantras, and follow its commandments, then you will be censored, banished, blacklisted, persecuted, and punished.
sentences.zh: 如果你不使用它的语言、不履行它的仪式、不背诵它的口号、不遵守它的诫命，你就会遭到审查、放逐、列入黑名单、迫害和惩罚。

sentences.en: It's not going to happen to us.
sentences.zh: 这种事不会发生在我们身上。

sentences.en: The Times reports that the speeches, delivered in front of Mount Rushmore and the White House,
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》报道称，这两场分别在拉什莫尔山和白宫前发表的演讲，

sentences.en: signaled that Trump would seek once again to exploit racial and cultural divisions in an effort to win re-election.
sentences.zh: 释放出一个信号：特朗普将再次试图利用种族和文化分歧，以争取赢得连任。

sentences.en: I am here as your president to proclaim before the country and before the world, this monument will never be desecrated.
sentences.zh: 我作为你们的总统，在此向全国和全世界庄严宣告：这座纪念碑绝不会被亵渎。

sentences.en: These heroes will never be defaced.
sentences.zh: 这些英雄的雕像绝不会被损毁。

sentences.en: Their legacy will never, ever be destroyed.
sentences.zh: 他们的传奇绝不会被摧毁。

sentences.en: Their achievements will never be forgotten.
sentences.zh: 他们的功绩绝不会被遗忘。

sentences.en: And Mount Rushmore will stand forever as an eternal tribute to our forefathers and to our freedom.
sentences.zh: 拉什莫尔山将永远巍然耸立，作为对我们先辈和我们自由的永恒敬意。

sentences.en: Neither event enforced social distancing rules, and both were held despite pleas from public health officials that they be canceled to avoid spreading the coronavirus.
sentences.zh: 这两场活动都没有执行社交距离规定，并且尽管公共卫生官员恳求取消以避免传播冠状病毒，它们还是照常举行了。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 以上就是本期《每日新闻》的全部内容。

sentences.en: I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: This week on The Wirecutter Show, we're getting ready for hosting over the holidays.
sentences.zh: 本周的《Wirecutter秀》将为您介绍如何为假期招待客人做好准备。

sentences.en: Tune in for tips on making your guests feel at home.
sentences.zh: 收听节目，获取让客人宾至如归的小贴士。

sentences.en: Are they a blackout sleeper?
sentences.zh: 他们对光线敏感、需要完全黑暗才能入睡吗？

sentences.en: I don't mean do they blackout to go to sleep.
sentences.zh: 我不是指他们是不是喝到不省人事才去睡觉。

sentences.en: I mean, what kind of light do they require?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们对光线有什么要求？

sentences.en: Because that is a very specific thing.
sentences.zh: 因为这是一个非常具体的问题。

sentences.en: Do they have allergies, food sensitivities?
sentences.zh: 他们有过敏症或食物敏感吗？

sentences.en: Are they coffee tea drinkers?
sentences.zh: 他们习惯喝咖啡还是茶？

sentences.en: What time do they like to get up?
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢几点起床？

sentences.en: Find The Wirecutter Show on the New York Times app or wherever you like to listen.
sentences.zh: 您可以在《纽约时报》应用程序上或您喜欢的任何播客平台上找到《Wirecutter秀》。
